commit f0575df148e7c6e9a952a9da601adb09536914db
Author: apopov <tank2.alex@...>
Date: 2018-03-02T09:54:39Z

IGNITE-7851: .NET: linq query throws Hexadecimal string with odd number of characters exception

isapego, skalashnikov
Please review the changes.

I force the key type assignment for QueryEntity in .NET code if it is not passed. Java code does not have similar CacheConfiguration constructor, so it is better to fix at .NET side.
ptupitsyn Could you please review as well

alexey.tank2, why is this ticket resolved? I've reopened it.

The fix is not correct, we can not infer SQL types from ICache generic arguments.
Generic arguments can be anything: interfaces, abstract classes, {{object}, etc etc.

There is nothing to fix, user HAS to specify key type as well as value type in such cases.

ptupitsyn, ok got it. Why do we have CacheConfiguration constructor in C# that makes users fill they do everything correct and get this error?

new CacheConfiguration("Person", typeof(Person))

BTW, Java part does not have such constructor.

Shall we deprecate it?

Discussed with vozerov. It was decided to deprecate the constructor

        public CacheConfiguration(string name, params Type[] queryTypes) : this(name)
        {
            QueryEntities = queryTypes.Select(type => new QueryEntity {ValueType = type}).ToArray();
        }

and update all the samples that use it.

Thanks,
Alexey
alexey.tank2 deprecating the constructor makes sense to me, please go ahead.
TC results are green. https://ci.ignite.apache.org/project.html?projectId=IgniteTests24Java8&branch_IgniteTests24Java8=pull%2F3595%2Fhead
alexey.tank2, looks good to me.
Looks good to me. Merged to master.
